raw_segments.text: Cadmus, on with your awful burden! Follow me, thralls, to his house, whose body grievously
with many a weary search at last in Dim Kithiran's glens I found, torn limb from limb, and through
the interweaving forest-weed scattered men told me of my daughter's deed, when I was
just returned within these walls, with grey terezias, from the bacchanals. And back I
hide me to the hills again to seek my murdered son.
There saw I plain Actaean's mother, ranging where he died, Autano, and Eno by her side,
wandering ghastly in the pine copses. Agavi was not there. The rumour is she cometh fleet-foot
Hithera. Tease true, a sight I scarce can bend mine eyes unto. Agavi turning from the palace
and seeing him. My father a great boast is thine this hour. Thou hast begotten daughters,
high in power and valiant above all mankindye, all valiant, though none like me.
I have let fall the shuttle by the loom, and raised my hand for higher things, to slay from
out thy land wild beasts. See, in mine arms I bear the prize, that nailed above these portals it may
rise to show what things thy daughters did. Do thou take it, and call a feast? Proud art thou now,
and highly favoured in our valiantcy.
